t:
(a) Creation of Fund for Redemption of Real Property.—Subchapter A of chapter 80 (relating to application of internal revenue laws) is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new section:


“SEC. 7810. 
REVOLVING FUND FOR REDEMPTION OF REAL PROPERTY.

“(a) 
Establishment of Fund.—There is established a revolving fund, under the control of the Secretary or his delegate, which shall be available without fiscal year limitation for all expenses necessary for the redemption (by the Secretary or his delegate) of real property as provided in section 7425(d) and section 2410 of title 28 of the United States Code. There are authorized to be appropriated from time to time such sums (not to exceed $1,000,000 in the aggregate) as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of this section.


“(b) 
Reimbursement of Fund.—The fund shall be reimbursed from the proceeds of a subsequent sale of real property redeemed by the United States in an amount equal to the amount expended out of such fund for such redemption.


“(c) 
System of Accounts.—The Secretary or his delegate shall maintain an adequate system of accounts for such fund and prepare annual reports on the basis of such accounts.”




 
    (b) 
Deposit of Money Received.—Section 7809 (relating to deposit of collections) is amended by striking out “and 7654,” in subsection (a) and inserting in lieu thereof “7654, and 7810,”; and by amending subsection (b)—

        (1) 
by striking out “and” at the end of paragraph (2),
 
        (2) 
by striking out the period at the end of paragraph (3) and inserting in lieu thereof “; and”, and
 
        (3) 
by inserting after paragraph (3) the following new paragraph:


“(4) 
Surplus proceeds in sales of redeemed property.—Surplus proceeds in any sale under section 7506 of real property redeemed by the United States, after making allowance for the amount of the tax, interest, penalties, and additions thereto, and for the costs of sale.”



  
    (c) 
Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections for subchapter A of chapter 80 is amended by adding at the end thereof the following:


“Sec. 7810. Revolving fund for redemption of real property.”.

fable.w: This section creates a revolving fund controlled by the Secretary for redeeming real property, with rules on reimbursement, accounts, and deposit of proceeds. The tempting reading is that the 'annual reports' or the 'delegate' language implies outside involvement, but the reports are internal accounting and the delegate is a federal official. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: There is established a revolving fund, under the control of the Secretary or his delegate

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a revolving fund for the redemption of real property and outlines internal accounting and reimbursement procedures. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are the Secretary of the Treasury and his delegates, who are federal officials.
qwen_block.s: There is established a revolving fund, under the control of the Secretary or his delegate, which shall be available without fiscal year limitation for all expenses necessary for the redemption (by the Secretary or his delegate) of real property

opus.w: This section creates a revolving fund for the Secretary to redeem real property and sets out how the fund is reimbursed and how its accounts are kept. The only reporting is internal annual accounting, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or consultation with outside parties. The cross-reference to 28 U.S.C. 2410 only describes when the fund can be used; it does not grant an outside party a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: The Secretary or his delegate shall maintain an adequate system of accounts for such fund and prepare annual reports on the basis of such accounts.
opus.b: Step 1 (thinking): The one tempting reading is the cross-reference to "section 2410 of title 28 of the United States Code," the provision that lets parties bring certain lien-related suits involving the United States. That might look like a right to sue. It fails because the section only cites that law to say when the redemption fund can be spent; it doesn't give any outside party a new right to sue over a federal decision. The rest of the section sets up an internal revolving fund, deals with reimbursement and accounting, and requires the Secretary to keep accounts and prepare annual reports. None of this involves anyone outside the federal government in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a revolving fund for the redemption of real property, controlled entirely by the Secretary of the Treasury or his delegate. All actors involved (the Secretary, his delegate, the United States) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with, coordinate with, or allow participation from any outside parties such as states, local governments, the public, or experts. The process described is internal administrative and financial management.
qwen_chat.s: There is established a revolving fund, under the control of the Secretary or his delegate, which shall be available without fiscal year limitation for all expenses necessary for the redemption (by the Secretary or his delegate) of real property as provided in section 7425(d) and section 2410 of title 28 of the United States Code.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Secretary or his delegate" involves some form of internal coordination or delegation that could be misconstrued as participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or officials is not participation. Furthermore, there is no mention of any outside party (state, local, public, expert, etc.) being consulted or involved in the decision-making process regarding the fund's establishment or operation. The text is purely about internal financial management and accounting within the federal government.
